ā + a → ā; the two words belong to different parts of the sentence (स्मृता to the speaker, अखिलाः to परमापदः).

sandhi.type: no change (final t before an unvoiced consonant)
sandhi.note: Final t stays unvoiced before p; the words are only written together. Inside परमापद्, परम + आपद् gives ā (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः, 6.1.101).

samasa.sense: instantly, the very moment I am remembered
the gravest misfortunes; the first member stands in its stem form परम-

morph.note: Simple future of the causative stem नाशय- (√नश् ‘perish’ → ‘cause to perish’) with the future marker -इष्य-: नाशय् + इष्य + आमि.
A feminine participle with the force of a condition: ‘(I,) being remembered’, i.e. ‘whenever I am remembered’. The Goddess is quoted speaking of herself.
Genitive for the recipient: वरः अस्माकं दत्तः, ‘a boon was given of us’ = ‘to us’, a common use of the genitive in place of the dative.

mantras.anvaya: तया अस्माकम् वरः दत्तः, यथा — आपत्सु स्मृता (अहम्) भवताम् अखिलाः परमापदः तत्क्षणात् नाशयिष्यामि (इति)।
mantras.anvaya_en: A passive main clause (तया … वरः दत्तः) followed by the boon in direct speech, introduced by यथा: the Goddess is the unexpressed subject of नाशयिष्यामि, and स्मृता is a participle of condition.
mantras.lit: By her a boon was given to us, that: ‘Remembered in calamities, I shall at that very moment destroy all your extreme calamities.’
mantras.tr: She gave us a boon: ‘When I am remembered in your misfortunes, I will that very instant destroy all your direst calamities.’
mantras.tr_note: The verse is the gods’ own thought, closed by इति in 5.7; the passive ‘was given by her’ is rendered as active.

comm.t: The gods recall the promise made at the end of the second story: they asked, संस्मृता संस्मृता त्वं नो हिंसेथाः परमापदः (4.36), and she consented (4.39). Here the same promise is quoted in her own voice, with the same word परमापदः.
A modern reading: the gods have lost everything except a promise, and their first act is to remember it. In this text remembrance is not a feeling but the condition on which help arrives.

sandhi.note: Final m becomes anusvāra before a consonant. -āḥ before the voiced h: the visarga becomes y, which is lost before a consonant.

samasa.sense: the Goddess as the māyā belonging to Viṣṇu (compare Hari’s Mahāmāyā, 1.55); the name returns in the first yā devī stanza (5.14–16)

morph.note: Perfect of √स्तु: the reduplicating syllable keeps the stop (तु-, not स्तु-), and the root’s s becomes ṣ after u (तुष्टु-); before the ending -उः the u becomes uv. With प्र: ‘they praised forth’.
Perfect of √गम्: reduplication ज- (g → j) and loss of the root vowel before the weak ending: ज-ग्म्-उः.
Absolutive: ‘having made (up their) mind’; the action precedes that of the main verb जग्मुः.

mantras.anvaya: इति मतिम् कृत्वा देवाः नगेश्वरम् हिमवन्तम् जग्मुः। ततः तत्र विष्णुमायाम् देवीम् प्रतुष्टुवुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two main verbs with one subject (देवाः): जग्मुः with its goal हिमवन्तम्, and प्रतुष्टुवुः with its object देवीम्; कृत्वा marks the prior resolve.
mantras.lit: Having made up their mind thus, the gods went to Himavat, lord of mountains; there, then, they praised the Goddess Viṣṇumāyā.
mantras.tr: Resolved on this, the gods went to the Himālaya, king of mountains, and there they sang the praises of the Goddess, Viṣṇumāyā.

comm.t: The gods go to the Himālaya and begin the hymn that runs from 5.9 to 5.82. The place matters to the story: it is there that Pārvatī comes to bathe (5.84) and that Ambikā comes forth from her body (5.85–87).
The name Viṣṇumāyā links this hymn to the first story, where the Goddess was Viṣṇu’s Yoganidrā and Mahāmāyā (1.54–55). The hymn’s first yā devī stanza names her by this very title (5.14–16).

morph.note: Perfect plural of √वच् with samprasāraṇa (va → u) in both the root and the reduplication: उ + उच् + उः → ऊचुः.

comm.t: The gods, on the Himālaya, begin their hymn to the Goddess (5.9–82), as Medhas reports it to Suratha.

Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

sandhi.type: visarga before an unvoiced consonant (no change)
sandhi.note: Before p the visarga stays. Before the s of स्म (प्रणताः स्म) it also stays, as optionally allowed before a sibilant.

samasa.sense: the Goddess as supreme among deities; महत् takes the form महा- as first member of a karmadhāraya

morph.note: Feminine i-stems may take the dative ending -ai (प्रकृत्यै) beside the general -aye (प्रकृतये). The hymn uses the -ai forms throughout (वृद्ध्यै, सिद्ध्यै, ख्यात्यै, कृत्यै), matching the ā- and ī-stems (शिवायै, देव्यै).
Past participle of प्र + √नम्: the nasal of the root is lost before -ta (नत), and n becomes ṇ after the r of प्र. With the accusative ताम्: ‘bowed to her’.
The same formula नताः स्म occurs in chapter 4 (4.3, 4.5). The participle needs a copula ‘we are’; the full verb appears elsewhere as स्मः (प्रपन्नाः स्मः, 2.8).

mantras.anvaya: देव्यै नमः, महादेव्यै शिवायै सततम् नमः। प्रकृत्यै भद्रायै नमः। नियताः (वयम्) ताम् प्रणताः स्म।
mantras.anvaya_en: Three salutations with नमः and the dative, then a statement of the speakers: (वयम्) नियताः ताम् प्रणताः स्म ‘we, restrained, are bowed to her’.
mantras.lit: Salutation to the Goddess, to the Great Goddess; to Śivā always salutation. Salutation to Prakṛti, to Bhadrā. Self-restrained, we have bowed to her.
mantras.tr: Homage to the Goddess, to the Great Goddess; to the Auspicious One, homage for ever. Homage to Nature, the Primal One, to the Gracious One. With minds held still we bow before her.
mantras.tr_note: ‘The Primal One’ makes explicit that प्रकृति here is the cosmic principle, not ‘nature’ in the everyday sense.

comm.t: The gods’ hymn opens with salutations in the dative: the Goddess is named as Devī, Mahādevī, Śivā (the auspicious), Prakṛti (the source of the manifest world) and Bhadrā (the benign). The last pāda turns from address to statement: the gods describe themselves as restrained and bowed.
The hymn of 5.9–82 is recited on its own in the Śākta tradition as the Tantrokta Devīsūkta. Its opening verse is among the most widely recited in the text.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also has the names 209, महादेवी, and 53, शिवा, and the related 397, मूलप्रकृतिः. The shared epithets belong to a common Śākta vocabulary; the two works are separate.

flags.uncertain: स्म: the printed short form is required by the metre (the seventh syllable of an even anuṣṭubh pāda must be light, which स्मः before ताम् would not be). As in 4.3 and 4.5 it is taken as स्मः ‘we are’ with the visarga lost metri causa; it may also be the particle स्म with the copula understood. The sense, ‘we bow to her’, is the same either way.
